mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
failure_condition: In a tightening regime, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the pre-tightening average (p > 0.10 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4% for two consecutive months, wage growth (PAYEMS) accelerates while industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat, signaling a strong labor market that crowds out equity valuations and depresses 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS growth > INDPRO growth for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Early signs of a labor market reacceleration
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is positive in at least 70% of similar labor-market trigger events (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) of more than 3% accompanied by a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3.0% for three months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as demand recovers without price pressure.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 3% for three consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 3.0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant excess returns in 100 analogous demand-inflation pairs (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month, while consumer demand (GDPC1) remains flat, predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as weak manufacturing signals a supply-side drag.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -5% while GDPC1 growth ≤ 0% in the same month
failure_condition: In 10 comparable supply-contraction events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (one-tailed p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% for 4 consecutive months, with no offsetting rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL), creates a low-rate, low-inflation environment that supports positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for four consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 3.5% for the same period
failure_condition: Across 20 such episodes, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than the 20-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a regime indicator) coincides with a sharp drop in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) of 10% in a month, producing a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market interprets labor market cooling as risk-off.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls > -10% in a single month (proxy for regime shift via labor data absence)
regime_hint: Labor market regime shift to cooling
failure_condition: Over 10 analogous negative PAYEMS shocks, the 5-day forward return is not persistently negative (p > 0.20 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in retail sales (HOUST) by more than 7% while industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat for two months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong retail demand supports optimism without supply bottlenecks.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 7% for two consecutive months AND INDPRO growth ≤ 0% for the same months
failure_condition: In 15 analogous demand-acceleration events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.5% for 6 consecutive months, absent a corresponding decline in interest rates (FEDFUNDS), suggests the Fed is holding policy steady and supports positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns via lower discounting of expected cash flows.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.5% for six consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS does not decline over the same period
failure_condition: Across 12 such steady low-inflation periods, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than the 20-day average (p > 0.05).
